title: World Bank reports Ukraine's economy contracted by 29.2 percent in 2022
body:
On 6 April 2023 the World Bank published a regional economic update for Europe and Central Asia that put Ukraine's gross domestic product contraction in 2022 at 29.2 percent. It projected growth of 0.5 percent in 2023 and said that the reopening of Black Sea ports, the resumption of grain trade and substantial donor support were helping to sustain economic activity.

The update also cited recent World Bank estimates that reconstruction and recovery would cost 411 billion US dollars, more than twice the size of Ukraine's pre-war economy in 2021.

Other institutions reported slightly different figures for the same contraction. The International Monetary Fund's press release of 31 March 2023 gave real GDP growth of minus 30.3 percent for 2022. Ukraine's Economy Ministry later reported, according to the Kyiv Independent on 18 November 2024, that GDP fell 29.1 percent in 2022, grew 5.3 percent in 2023 and grew 4.2 percent year on year in the first ten months of 2024. The differences reflect the vintage and method of each estimate rather than disagreement about the scale of the fall.
